source.title: The Singular Values of Convolutional Layers
source.authors: Hanie Sedghi; Vineet Gupta; Philip M. Long

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures convolutional-layer singular values and tests operator-norm regularization on CIFAR-10. It does not test whether gradient-based training from random initialization reaches near-zero training classification error or the conditions named in V1–V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 test error and training loss under operator-norm clipping, plus singular-value measurements of a pretrained ResNet. These do not measure the training classification error, convergence behavior, initialization, depth, learning-rate stability, or batch-normalization speed named by the claim versions. Mentioned initialization and normalization work is cited prior work, not this study's own result.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates convolutional singular-value computation and operator-norm regularization. Its test-error results, training-loss plots and pretrained-layer spectra do not test the outcomes or comparisons specified by V1–V6. Initialization and gradient propagation motivate the work, but are not experimentally tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors characterize convolutional singular values, enable efficient computation and operator-norm projection, and find improved CIFAR-10 test error. They conclude that operator-norm regularization and batch normalization complement each other; they do not establish the training outcomes specified by V1–V6.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes and evaluates exact singular-value computation and operator-norm projection as a regularizer; the listed claim versions concern training-error outcomes and training dynamics.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported CIFAR-10 test error varies with clipping threshold and whether clipping is used; the study also varies batch normalization and hyperparameter combinations in separate experiments. These are regularization outcomes, not outcomes named by the claim versions.

fits_no_version.finding: For a 32-layer CIFAR-10 ResNet, clipping every 100 steps at 0.5 or 1.0 produced test errors of 5.3% or 5.5%, versus 6.2% without clipping; clipping at 0.1 produced 6.7%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Operator-norm clipping can improve generalization, depending on the clipping threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: Hyperparameter sweeps showed improved best test performance and greater robustness with operator-norm regularization without batch normalization; regularization also helped with batch normalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Operator-norm regularization can improve test performance across hyperparameter choices and complement batch normalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Reshaped-kernel clipping every 100 steps matched the exact method's best accuracy. Clipping every step gave slightly worse best accuracy; the exact method took 11004 seconds versus 14490 seconds for reshaped-kernel clipping over 10000 batches.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Exact operator-norm clipping can match reshaped-kernel clipping in accuracy and run faster in the tested implementation.

fits_no_version.finding: Pretrained ResNet convolutional layers had different singular-value spectra and effective ranks, with the largest operator norms closest to the input.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolutional operator spectra vary across layers of a trained ResNet.

record.problems: The CIFAR-10 regularization experiment reports test error and training-loss plots, not training classification error. Results in the hyperparameter sweeps are plotted without numerical values in the supplied text. The paper says the reshaped-kernel comparison is only one dataset and may not generalize.
record.rows_left_out: No results meet the row rule for the claim versions: the reported test-error, training-loss and singular-value outcomes do not measure the behaviors those versions name.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels, and dependence on model size, stopping or regularization. Figure 2 reports training loss without readable endpoint values establishing training classification error.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization alternatives.
Effects of activation-matched, Gaussian or orthogonal initialization on training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery or divergence relative to an initial stability threshold and sharpness evolution during training. The learning-rate sweeps do not measure these quantities.

Matched comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and Fixup training. The separate hyperparameter sweeps report test error using different learning-rate grids.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation should change from tests to discusses; T6 is appropriate. There are no extracted rows to fix and no omitted claim-bearing results requiring rows.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sufficiently large convolutional networks reach zero or near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels, and how size, stopping, or regularization affect it.
Whether student width relative to teacher width changes spurious minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Whether depth raises training error in plain networks, whether shortcuts prevent it, and whether special initialization or normalization-free residual training changes that result.
Whether activation-matched or orthogonal initializations change training speed or trainable depth, including very deep tanh and convolutional networks.
Whether above-stability learning rates recover to low training loss, whether sharpness approaches a stability threshold, or whether runs diverge below it.
Whether batch normalization speeds accuracy gains or permits higher learning rates, and whether Fixup residual networks train comparably without normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
